title: Schema-weighted chaos probe for constrained decoder recovery and telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: validate and harden our constrained-decoder path when faced with adversarial/edge-case token emissions during streaming JSON-mode sessions. This ticket builds a schema-weighted chaos test harness that injects token-level perturbations, truncated stream fragments, interleaved toolcall markers, and deliberate sentinel collisions to exercise recovery and fallback logic in the runtime and client SDKs. Scope: regression harness, telemetry instrumentation, automated pass/fail scoring, and a short runbook for on-call escalation. Not in scope: model training changes or long-running exhaustive corpora generation (those are separate experiments).
motivation: We have observed intermittent schema deserialization errors in production when partial streaming outputs contain malformed fragments or when historic sentinel tokens appear in content. On high-throughput hosts the constrained-decoder fallback and the streaming reassembly logic must be resilient without increasing tail latency. This harness is intended to catch regressions early and provide signal for automatic rollbacks and alerting thresholds.
acceptance_criteria:
- Harness runs end-to-end against local runtime and a small fleet of dedicated staging GPUs and produces deterministic reports.
- At least three adversarial generators implemented: token-flip, sentinel-echo, truncated-mid-object.
- Pass/fail scoring: structured output compliance >= 99.3% for allowed noise level; failure triggers detailed diff blob and telemetry event.
- Streaming reassembly tests validate KV-cache continuity and toolcall boundary preservation in 10,000 simulated sessions.
- Telemetry emits a schema_violation metric with tags: model, route, latency_bucket, seed.
- A short runbook created with rollback and mitigation steps and linked PRs and dashboards.
- No binary or large datasets checked into repo; artifacts are uploaded to the build artifacts store with links in test reports.
test_plan:
1) Implement three adversarial generators (described below).
2) Wire generators into the existing streaming-test harness and add a schema-weighted sampler that biases mutations toward high-risk keys (IDs, timestamps, tool_call markers).
3) Create 10x mini-scenarios with varying sequence lengths and model families (gpt-style, vicuna-style, open-llama-style) using runtime-1.22.
4) Execute runs across small staging fleet and collect telemetry.
5) Compute compliance metrics and generate per-seed artifacts (raw stream, reassembled JSON, decoder logs).
6) Failures create GitHub issues automatically with artifacts linked.
7) Run daily for the next two weeks as part of CI smoke jobs; promote to weekly if stable.
adversarial_generators: token-flip: randomly flip high-probability tokens near JSON punctuation and string boundaries
sentinel-echo: inject repeated toolcall sentinel tokens within string fields and inside arrays
truncate-mid-object: cut the stream mid-object and resume with a slightly altered schema variant to force decoder backoff and fallback paths
telemetry_requirements: Emit structured telemetry events with the following fields: seed, generator_type, mutation_rate, model_family, route, latency_ms, schema_violation=true/false, recovered_via_fallback=true/false. Events should be ingested into the staging observability dashboard under 'structured-output/harness' and expose an alert rule when schema_violation rate > 0.7% over 1h with severity P1.
observability_dashboards: Create a lightweight Grafana panel that shows: compliance_over_time, schema_violation_rate_by_model, average_recovery_latency, top-10 failing seeds. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood/boards/structured-output-harness (placeholder)
runbook: If an automated run fails and schema_violation rate spikes: 1) Triage logs for seed and generator_type. 2) If failure is isolated to a single runtime binary version, trigger canary rollback to previous runtime-1.21. 3) If widespread across models, set routing fallback policy to serve non-streaming typed fallback for the impacted route and notify PM/owner. 4) Create incident record and attach artifacts from harness. 5) Post-mortem within 72 hours if customer-facing impact discovered.
implementation_notes:
- Reuse the streaming harness plumbing but add a mutation layer between model token emitter and streaming reassembly layer.
- Keep mutations deterministic per seed to enable reproducible failures.
- Use schema-weighted sampling: keys with high customer impact (id, email, order_id, tool_call) get higher mutation probability.
- Instrument the constrained decoder to emit an event whenever it takes a fallback path, including decoder state snapshot pointers (no PII).
- Add a small compatibility shim in SDKs that attempts graceful reassembly when a partial stream fails initial parse; the shim will attempt up to 3 heuristic repairs before surfacing an error.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Tests could introduce noise into shared staging telemetry. Mitigation: tag all events with harness=true and keep retention short.
- Risk: Deterministic seeds could bias coverage. Mitigation: run both seeded and pseudo-random batches.
- Risk: Heuristic SDK repairs might mask real regressions. Mitigation: require a telemetry flag 'heuristic_repair_used' and include these runs in a separate report bucket.
